messages:
maria: heads-up — after the streaming-chunk split change in the gateway (deploy @ 1812340000) we're seeing host-side CPU p95 jump ~2x for short chat requests. low QPS but huge spikes. :eyes:
kevin: saw the alert. any flamegraphs yet?
josh: I grabbed a quick profile on a repro box, looks like tokenization + gRPC framing is burning cycles when chunks are sub-100 bytes. attaching sample log: 
```
[2026-05-14T15:42:10Z] req=abc123 duration=45ms host_cpu_ms=30 tokenize_ms=18 grpc_write_ms=10 kvcache_lookup_ms=1
[2026-05-14T15:42:11Z] req=abc124 duration=120ms host_cpu_ms=90 tokenize_ms=60 grpc_write_ms=20 kvcache_lookup_ms=5
```

kevin: interesting — tokenize_ms scales superlinearly with tiny chunking. maybe we added extra copies during framing. did the new framer allocate buffers per-chunk?
tina: it does, because we tried to avoid a big coalesce step. change was in https://git.redwood/infra/patches/xyz — line 87: we moved from coalescing to streaming-slice to reduce tail latency.
maria: right but the profiler shows extra memcpy in host path. also seen more gRPC WINDOW_UPDATE churn — HTTP/2 window updates every chunk, which steals CPU and serializes writes.
josh: kvcache behavior is weird too — small prefix hits are thrashing the cache metadata lock. when requests are chunked aggressively, each chunk triggers a K-V lookup because of our prefix normalization timing. lock contention reports spike.
kevin: rough plan: revert streaming-slice flag, re-enable coalescing for requests < 512 bytes, and add a fast-path tokenizer that avoids copying when input is already in contiguous buffer. can we patch gate?
tina: I can flip a runtime flag: `gateway.streaming_coalesce_threshold=512` and `gateway.enable_copyless_tokenizer=false` for canary.
maria: please do canary to 10% in eu-west1 only. also add verbose metrics: host_tokenize_calls, host_memcpy_bytes, http2_window_updates.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: canary roll to eu-west1 (10%) by tina at 15:55 UTC — build #build-2026-556.
josh: quick mitigation script i used locally to reproduce: 
```
# repro script: send many short streaming requests
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -N -H "Content-Type: application/grpc+proto" \
    -d $'\x00\x00\x00test' http://gateway.internal/v1/stream && sleep 0.05
done
```
kevin: thanks. once canary is up I'll run the same script vs canary and control. if p95 drops back, we confirmed it. if not, next is instrument kernel selection path for memcpy vs zero-copy, and check batching heuristic changes after framer.
tina: canary started. enabling metrics tagged `canary/stream-coalesce-512`.
maria: also record KV cache metrics: lock_wait_ms, lookup_count, eviction_rate — I suspect metadata lock hot-path.
josh: note for followup: batching heuristics may be impacted because we relied on chunk boundaries to form batch keys. if chunking changes distribution, batch size variance increases and kernel selection may pick suboptimal kernels for short sequences. add `batch_size_histogram` to the trace.
kevin: agree — add that to the rollout dashboard. if we need a quick code revert, i'll open a PR to reintroduce an explicit coalesce stage in the framer and reuse the existing zero-copy tokenizer connectors.
maria: thanks team. action items: tina — canary toggle + metrics (done), kevin — open revert PR if canary doesn't help, josh — run repro and attach flamegraph to the thread, i'll follow up with SLO impact note. 
kevin: tentative cause summary: aggressive streaming-slice + per-chunk gRPC writes -> more memcpys + HTTP2 window updates + KV metadata lock thrash -> higher host CPU p95 and worse tail latency.
ci-bot: canary rollout succeeded to 10% at 15:58 UTC.
josh: initial numbers vs control: p95 host_cpu reduced from 92ms -> 38ms for short requests on canary. allocating full run now, will paste flamegraph link.
maria: excellent. keep this thread for postmortem notes and decision.
